newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Buyers said shifting to Malaysia from Thai rubber.
newsitem.headline: Buyers said shifting to Malaysia from Thai rubber.

text.p: The rubber trade was said to be shifting its attention on Monday to Malaysian rubber and away from Thai rubber as the high support price in Bangkok gave Malaysian-origins a discount in the market, dealers said.

"There is a shift underway to Malaysian rubber. Anybody who can use TSR rubber to replace RSS3 rubber are doing so," a trader said, adding the average price of TSR rubber reached US$1.04/05 a kg against the $1.15/kg quote for RSS3 rubber.
TSR rubber is similar to the technically specified rubber produced by Malaysia while the RSS3 grade rubber is the main grade rubber produced by Thailand.

The decision by the Thai government to raise its support price for RSS3 rubber in the last two weeks to 29 baht/kg from 27.50 baht previously has prompted "some buyers to look for cheaper alternatives such as Malaysia," another trader said.
"Malaysian rubber is now on average about 10 (U.S.) cents cheaper than Thai rubber," a dealer said.
Action in the Singapore rubber market remained thin by midday with most waiting leads in the afternoon, traders said. "There was nothing at all in the market this morning," one said.
At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 116.00 U.S. cents a kg from 115.00 cents. - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
